scope: First check of the batch. The diff is git -C ~/Dropbox/ErgodicGFN arXiv/source diff against HEAD a9c3b9d: an uncommitted working tree, main.tex only, 15 insertions and 9 deletions, 6 hunks. The batch is C-47, C-44 and C-45 of papers/egf/programme/corrections.toml (batch T-egf-correct-captions). All three are kind typo, status adopted, basis DEC-141, added_hypotheses [], with no anchor and no refutation. Nothing is stated in Lean, so 'faithful' here means two things: the applied text is the entry's corrected text, and the edit is true of the figure it captions. v1 is papers/egf/legacy/orig/main.tex. tools/corrections.py check --v2 <working copy> reports '49 entries, all rules hold'. Line numbers are v2 (the working copy) unless marked v1.

entries.notes:
v2 l.961 is the corrected text verbatim. It replaces v1 l.899, 'NLL estimation for a range of values of $k$ ...', which is exactly the deleted line.

I read images/filter_cutoff.jpg directly. The horizontal axis is labelled 'Filter cutoff factor', with ticks from -2.0 to 2.0. The vertical axis is also labelled 'Filter cutoff factor', with ticks from -2.2 to -1.2. The curve is flat at about -1.06 for k >= 0.4. It falls steeply to a minimum of about -2.16 near k = -0.4, then rises jaggedly to about -1.63 at k = -2. So the parenthesis 'both axes are labelled `Filter cutoff factor'' is literally true, including the capitalisation.

The horizontal axis is k. By l.947 the threshold is f_sat = m - k sigma, so a large k gives a low threshold and nothing is cut. That is the flat plateau on the right of the image.

The vertical axis is the NLL. v1's caption already named the NLL as the plotted quantity. l.956 says k is chosen by recomputing the NLL. And ~/egf-reproduction/results/T-egf-repro-torus-il/REPORT.md section 4, finding 1, reproduces the shape: flat for large k, a dip, then a jagged rise as validation points are cut. Negative values are possible for the NLL of a density. Reading the values as a log-likelihood would make the filter's 'optimal filter value' (l.965) the worst value, so the NLL reading is the coherent one.

The caption adds nothing beyond naming the two axes and quoting the label. It keeps v1's 'for a given model on the volcano dataset'.

The figure has no \label and no reference points to it. It renders as Figure 4 on p.16, and the caption now takes two lines.

added_hypotheses = [] and none was added. As a typo, it has no refutation.

There are six sites, each matching the corrected text, and each deleted line equals its v1 printed line.

(1) v1 l.1022 is now v2 l.1087. It reads '... on the torus $\mathbb T^2$, i.e.\ two generators of $\mathrm{SL}(2,\mathbb Z)$ together with their inverses. ... but some under densities.' That is the corrected text, including the comma before 'i.e.', the control space after it, and the final period. It renders on p.18 as 'torus T², i.e. two generators of SL(2, Z) together with their inverses. ... some under densities.' It is true of the figure: four moves are two generators plus their two inverses.

(2) v1 l.1209 and l.1309 are now v2 l.1276 and l.1378. 'lest stable' becomes 'less stable'.

(3) v1 l.1211 and l.1311 are now v2 l.1278 and l.1380. '2 hidden layer of width 32' becomes '2 hidden layers of width 32'.

(4) v1 l.1364 is now v2 l.1435. '2spirals' becomes 'two spirals'. This is the subcaption of the two-spirals subfigure a, whose panels are ablation/2spiral/2x32 to 9x32.

Nothing else on these lines changed, as the word diff and the pdftotext diff show. The finding's v2 line numbers (l.1060, l.1248, ...) are from before later shifts. That is historical and needs no change. The same slips in the two-spirals main caption are C-45's, as the entry says.

added_hypotheses = [] and none was added. As a typo, it has no refutation.

v1 l.1412 is now v2 l.1485, and v1 l.1414 is now v2 l.1487. Both are the corrected text as the register now holds it, with 'in the second subfigure'. The diff is 'width' -> 'widths', ', with 4x128 and 5x128 in the second subfigure', 'lest' -> 'less', 'layer' -> 'layers' and ', and 4x128 and 5x128'.

The edit is true of the figure.

Subfigure a (l.1397-1435) holds eight panels of 0.24\linewidth, which set four to a row: 2x32, 3x32, 4x32 and 5x32 on top, 6x32 to 9x32 below.

Subfigure b (l.1439-1481) holds 2x64, 3x64, 4x128 and 5x128 on top, and 6x64, 7x64, 8x64 and 9x64 below. ablation/2spiral/ has no 4x64.png or 5x64.png. The PNGs carry no size label, so the file names are the only evidence for the sizes, and nothing contradicts them. The rendered p.21 shows the subfigures labelled 'a' and 'b', each two rows of four.

So '4x128 and 5x128 in the second subfigure' is right. 'In the second row', the adopted text before the master's change, would have been wrong: the second row on the page is subfigure a's bottom row, 6x32 to 9x32. The master's change is the fix, and the marker records it.

The main caption and subcaption b (l.1481, C-37) now agree. 'The 9x64 experiment' exists: it is b's last panel.

One residual point, not a finding. The range '2x32 to 9x64' in the main caption does not itself say that 4x64 and 5x64 were not shown. Subcaption b, directly above, says it, so the figure as a whole is unambiguous. This is the adopted text.

build.notes:
I ran latexmk -pdf -interaction=nonstopmode -halt-on-error main.tex in /tmp copies, never in the working copy. The working-copy copy was built from the tracked files via git ls-files, and its main.tex was cmp-identical. HEAD a9c3b9d came from git archive. In both, main.bbl was removed so that bibtex ran.

Results:
- Both builds exit 0 with 21 pages.
- No undefined reference or citation, no rerun request and no error after the final pass.
- bibtex reports 0 warnings, and the regenerated main.bbl is byte-identical to the tracked one.
- Overfull and Underfull lines are identical across the two logs.
- The aux newlabel lines differ only in the caption-title fields of fig:minimal_checker, fig:size_star, fig:size_circles and fig:size_spirals. Their numbers (7, 8, 9, 10) and pages (18, 19, 20, 21) are unchanged.
- The warnings are the same in both builds: amsthm 'Unknown theoremstyle fact', hyperref 'Ignoring empty anchor', and one pdfTeX 'destination with the same identifier (name{equation.3})' on p.3.

The pdfTeX warning is pre-existing. It is also present in builds of f3a75ad and of the camera-ready 4e74ce4, so it does not come from this batch (aside for the planner: a duplicate hyperref anchor equation.3).

I rendered and read pp.16, 18 and 21.

All /tmp copies were deleted (egfcheck-v2, -base, -prev, -cr and -png). The working copy is untouched: main.tex md5 dd643c5e… and its mtime are as before, and git status still shows ' M main.tex' plus the ignored main.pdf.

Aside: the working copy's main.pdf (21:11:48) and tracked main.bbl (21:11:45) are newer than main.tex (21:11:33), so someone built in place before this check. main.bbl is byte-identical to git, so nothing reaches the diff.
